subject: Re: Post-call: model fit + quality regression concerns / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@retailco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-10T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call recap: model fit & next steps

Jordan — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary from discovery:
- Primary goal: improve customer support triage accuracy for RetailCo chat volume (short, transactional queries).
- Current pain: recent model update appears to have introduced a quality regression on short-form intents (higher false-positive routing to Tier 2).
- Success metric: intent classification precision >= 92% on the RetailCo prompt set; latency target 150ms p95.

Redwood recommendations (initial):
1) Candidate models: redwood-embed-v1.10 (for reranking + embeddings) + redwood-chat-small-1.11 for live intents (we want a fast, quantized variant).
2) Eval artifacts: shared initial eval report + prompt set for RetailCo (attached). Please review the "redwood-eval-report-20260210.pdf" and the prompt_set_v2.txt.
3) Short-term: pin traffic for RetailCo to model redwood-chat-small@v1.11 in production while we run a canary of v1.12 on a 5% cohort.
4) If you prefer rollback, we can execute a rollback to v1.11 immediately with a one-hour scheduled window and a QA checklist.

Next steps (I propose):
- You: confirm whether you want immediate rollback or a pinned canary.
- Us: Rishi will share diffs and a lightweight action plan for pinning/rollback + a mutual action plan (MAP) for implementation.
- Schedule 30-min follow-up this week to review the eval diffs and agree on timing.

Attachments: redwood-eval-report-20260210.pdf (summary), prompt_set_v2.txt (RetailCo test prompts), benchmark-diffs-v1.11-v1.12.csv (initial perf diffs).

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior AE, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

Redwood Inference — Production-first LLM inference

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@retailco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@retailco.com>
Date: 2026-02-11T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: model fit & next steps

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A couple quick clarifying notes: 

- We started seeing the spike in Tier 2 escalations after last week's push (you mentioned v1.12). Our SREs flagged the change on Feb 6.
- For us, immediate business priority is minimizing customer impact; if rollback is low-friction we'd prefer that while you run the canary.
- Before we approve any rollback window, procurement wants the expected downtime/risk summary and a short MAP so they can sign off.

Could Rishi share:
- The concrete precision/recall diffs on the RetailCo prompt set between v1.11 and v1.12;
- Any known root-cause notes for the regression (is it prompting sensitivity, generation length, or tokenization changes?).

Happy to do a quick sync — I'm available Wed/Thu mornings.

Jordan
Product Ops | RetailCo

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@retailco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-12T11:26:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: model fit & next steps

Jordan — quick technical note and summary of the initial diffs (see attached CSV + shared Drive link):

Findings (short):
- Precision on RetailCo prompt_set_v2:
  - v1.11: 93.4%
  - v1.12: 88.9%
- Most regressions are concentrated on short, ambiguous utterances (2–5 tokens) where the model started preferring a Tier 2 escalation intent.
- Latency: v1.12 shows a 10% improvement p95 in some paths (we used a new attention kernel) but that change seems correlated with prompt truncation behavior for short inputs.

Root cause hypothesis:
- Kernel selection + small tokenizer changes in v1.12 altered some boundary tokenization for terse prompts; that produced subtle shifts in the final logits for edge intents. Not a data drift issue — introduced with the model binary change.

Options: 
1) Rollback to v1.11 immediately — low-risk, restore observed precision to prior baseline. We can schedule a 30–60 minute window; rollback is a config change, not infra-level.
2) Pin production traffic to v1.11 while we run a 5% canary of v1.12 and push a micro-patch to address tokenizer handling.
3) If you prefer a code-level short-term mitigation: apply a prompt post-processing step to rewrite ambiguous 2–5 token utterances with a conservative reranking rule (we can ship an edge rule in 1–2 business days).

Attachments: benchmark-diffs-v1.11-v1.12.csv (detailed per-prompt diffs), prompt_set_v2.txt (retailco prompts), redwood-eval-report-20260210.pdf.

Action items I can own this week: 
- Create a MAP for rollback + sign-off doc for Procurement (includes expected impact, rollback steps, and verification checklist).
- Run an expedited canary with logs and sample diffs visible in the shared Drive link: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/retailco-evals-20260210

Let me know if you want us to proceed with rollback or the pin+canary.

— Rishi
Principal Inference Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@retailco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-13T08:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: model fit & next steps

Jordan — from a CS/ops perspective, rollback is the least disruptive to your customers (restores baseline). If Procurement needs the MAP, we'll circulate a short doc that includes: scope, rollback window, verification steps (sampled intent checks + 30-min post-rollback monitoring), and SLA impact (none expected).

If you opt for pin+canary we recommend this schedule: 
- Day 0: Pin to v1.11 for 100% traffic (fast).
- Day 1: Launch 5% canary to v1.12 in staging-like route; collect 24h of signals (precision, error rates, p95 latency).
- Day 2: Review results; if improvement in latency is worth the impact we can plan a micro-patch and revalidate.

I'll prepare the MAP and procurement sign-off doc. Marissa — can you coordinate the preferred rollback window with Jordan? Jordan — what time windows does Procurement allow for config rollbacks (business hours vs maintenance window)?

Thanks — Monica
Customer Success | Redwood Inference

Jordan — following up with next steps per the thread: 

1) Proposed immediate action: schedule rollback to v1.11 on Thu 2026-02-19 at 02:00–02:30 PT (30 minute window). This is a configuration rollback; expected customer-facing impact is minimal and we will monitor for 60 minutes post-rollback.
2) Procurement MAP: Rishi and Monica will circulate the sign-off doc by EOD today (includes rollback steps, risk, verification checklist).
3) Post-rollback plan: run canary on v1.12 at 5% for 48 hours with the prompt_set_v2 and the benchmark diffs visible on the Drive link. If we can patch the tokenizer handling and validate precision >= 92% we can rehearse a controlled rollout.

Please confirm the 02:00–02:30 PT slot or propose an alternative. Once Jordan confirms, I'll open the change with SRE and share the DocuSign/Procurement link for sign-off: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/8342

Thanks everyone — Marissa
